candidate_sources.name: EOG Global VIIRS Gas Flaring Database
candidate_sources.provider: Earth Observation Group, Payne Institute for Public Policy, Colorado School of Mines
candidate_sources.geographic_coverage: Global (Permian, Bakken, North Sea, Persian Gulf, Niger Delta, Jamnagar, etc.)
candidate_sources.temporal_coverage: 2012–present (annual catalog updates; monthly Nightfire VNF daily detections)
candidate_sources.spatial_precision: Point centroids (< 50 m precision) derived from multi-year Nightfire Planck fits
candidate_sources.temporal_precision: Aggregated annually for persistent flare stacks; individual VNF detections have sub-minute overpass times
candidate_sources.download_api: Direct CSV/KMZ download via EOG Portal; Google Earth Engine collection (NOAA/VIIRS/DNB/ANNUAL_V21)
candidate_sources.license_restrictions: EOG Data Use Agreement (updated 2025); free for academic/research with formal citation
candidate_sources.potential_circularity: LOW. Nightfire uses VIIRS M-bands (M7, M8, M10, M12, M13) with Planck blackbody curve fitting; FIRMS active fire uses I-bands (I4, I5) thresholding. Provides independent flare stack coordinates.
candidate_sources.major_limitations: Identifies flare site location and multi-year flaring intensity, but does not provide instantaneous operational on/off status for a specific 15-minute window without matching to daily Nightfire VNF.
candidate_sources.recommended_use: AUTHORITATIVE T2 FLARE CENTROID SOURCE for expanding flare diversity beyond Jamnagar to the Permian Basin (US), North Sea (UK/Norway), and Middle East.

candidate_sources.name: WFIGS Interagency Fire Perimeters & IRWIN Incident Records
candidate_sources.provider: National Interagency Fire Center (NIFC) / USFS / BLM / IRWIN
candidate_sources.spatial_precision: GIS vector polygons mapped via airborne infrared (NIROPS), GPS ground walk, or Sentinel/Landsat burn mapping (< 30 m boundary accuracy)
candidate_sources.temporal_precision: Sub-daily perimeter timestamps, exact IRWIN incident report dates/times
candidate_sources.download_api: ArcGIS REST FeatureServer API / GeoJSON direct download (ArcGIS Hub)
candidate_sources.license_restrictions: US Public Domain / Creative Commons Zero (CC0)
candidate_sources.estimated_useful_events: 5,000+ documented wildfire incidents with verified GIS perimeters
candidate_sources.potential_circularity: NONE. Perimeters are operational tactical boundaries produced by incident management teams and airborne infrared aircraft, independent of NASA FIRMS active fire detection.
candidate_sources.major_limitations: Perimeters represent cumulative burned footprints at a given operational briefing period, not instantaneous flame lines. Internal unburned islands may be included within outer perimeter.
candidate_sources.recommended_use: AUTHORITATIVE T1 BENCHMARK for US wildfire ground truth. Expansion to additional years (2023–2025) and states.

candidate_sources.name: Canadian National Fire Database (CNFDB) & CWFIS Perimeters
candidate_sources.provider: Canadian Forest Service, Natural Resources Canada (NRCan)
candidate_sources.geographic_coverage: Canada (all 10 provinces and 3 territories, boreal & subarctic forests)
candidate_sources.temporal_coverage: 1980–2023 (annual release; live season monitoring via CWFIS)
candidate_sources.spatial_precision: GIS polygon perimeters from provincial fire management agencies
candidate_sources.temporal_precision: Report date, out date, start date (daily resolution)
candidate_sources.download_api: Direct Shapefile/GeoJSON download via Open Government Canada portal
candidate_sources.potential_circularity: NONE. Provincial forest service ground/aerial GPS boundary mapping.
candidate_sources.major_limitations: Annual official validation lag (typically 6-12 months); intra-event fire progression requires CWFIS daily maps.
candidate_sources.recommended_use: AUTHORITATIVE T1 SOURCE for international boreal forest wildfire expansion (Canada 2023 record fire season).

candidate_sources.name: NASA VIIRS Burned Area Product (VNP64A1 / MCD64A1)
candidate_sources.provider: NASA Land Processes DAAC (LP DAAC) / University of Maryland
candidate_sources.spatial_precision: 375 m pixel grid with Julian burn date
candidate_sources.temporal_precision: Estimated day of burn (approx. +/- 1 to 2 days)
candidate_sources.download_api: NASA Earthdata / LP DAAC HDF5 files / Google Earth Engine
candidate_sources.potential_circularity: HIGH CIRCULARITY RISK. VNP64A1 uses VIIRS active fire detections as training/seed inputs to identify surface reflectance change. Cannot serve as independent ground truth for active FIRMS pixels.
candidate_sources.major_limitations: Represents post-fire surface char/ash scar, not instantaneous flaming emitter. Strong methodological circularity with FIRMS.
candidate_sources.recommended_use: DO NOT USE AS PRIMARY GROUND TRUTH. Only permissible as secondary corroboration for spatial containment of unverified thermal anomalies.

candidate_sources.name: ICAR-IARI CREAMS Stubble Burning Monitoring Bulletin
candidate_sources.provider: Division of Agricultural Physics, Indian Agricultural Research Institute (IARI), New Delhi
candidate_sources.geographic_coverage: India (Punjab, Haryana, Uttar Pradesh, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh)
candidate_sources.spatial_precision: District and block-level summaries; daily event point coordinates
candidate_sources.temporal_precision: Daily bulletin based on satellite overpasses
candidate_sources.download_api: Daily PDF bulletins published online at creams.iari.res.in; no automated open GIS vector API
candidate_sources.potential_circularity: FATAL CIRCULARITY. CREAMS active fire points are generated by running NASA FIRMS / VIIRS / MODIS algorithms over Indian cropland masks. Training an ML model on FIRMS using CREAMS labels is predicting FIRMS from FIRMS.
candidate_sources.major_limitations: Zero independent ground verification in standard bulletin. Points are satellite thermal anomalies filtered by agricultural land-use.
candidate_sources.recommended_use: PROHIBITED AS SUPERVISED GROUND TRUTH. Only permissible for district-level temporal burn season contextual reference.

candidate_sources.name: Punjab Crop Residue Burning Information & Management System (CRBIMS)
candidate_sources.provider: Punjab Remote Sensing Centre (PRSC), Ludhiana / CAQM
candidate_sources.spatial_precision: Village-level administrative revenue boundary / parcel mapping
candidate_sources.independent_of_firms: PARTIALLY (ground squad verification reports are independent; daily map layers use VIIRS)
candidate_sources.download_api: State GIS portal (http://gis-prsc.punjab.gov.in/residue); access restricted to administrative users
candidate_sources.license_restrictions: Government departmental access; requires formal RTI or data sharing agreement with PRSC/CPCB
candidate_sources.potential_circularity: MODERATE. Flying squads are dispatched based on satellite alerts, but physical field verification logs record confirmed burnt area, crop type (paddy/wheat), and farmer challans.
candidate_sources.major_limitations: Ground verification records are administrative/legal files, not open data APIs. Exact sub-hour ignition time is rarely recorded.
candidate_sources.recommended_use: CONDITIONAL T2 TARGET. Requires targeted manual FOI/RTI acquisition or research partnership with PRSC/CPCB for physical inspection logs.

candidate_sources.name: Kansas Flint Hills Smoke Management Prescribed Agricultural Burning Registry
candidate_sources.provider: Kansas Department of Health and Environment (KDHE) / Kansas State University
candidate_sources.geographic_coverage: United States (Kansas Flint Hills tallgrass prairie & agricultural rangeland)
candidate_sources.spatial_precision: County and township/range section coordinates (1 square mile / 2.6 km² precision) with rancher burn permits
candidate_sources.download_api: Public dashboard / KDHE annual open data reports / GIS burn permit clearinghouse
candidate_sources.estimated_useful_events: 200–500 documented rangeland burn permits per season
candidate_sources.potential_circularity: NONE. Ground-issued rancher burn permits logged with local fire dispatch prior to ignition.
candidate_sources.major_limitations: Spatial precision is typically Public Land Survey System (PLSS) section centroid (1 mile grid), requiring spatial intersection with VIIRS footprint.
candidate_sources.recommended_use: VIABLE T1/T2 CANDIDATE FOR NON-FOREST VEGETATION / CONTROLLED AG-RANGELAND BURNING. Serves as clean non-circular vegetation fire benchmark.

candidate_sources.name: U.S. Chemical Safety and Hazard Investigation Board Incident Database
candidate_sources.provider: U.S. Chemical Safety Board (CSB), Washington, D.C.
candidate_sources.geographic_coverage: United States (refineries, petrochemical complexes, chemical plants, terminals)
candidate_sources.spatial_precision: Facility physical street address / gate coordinates (geocodable to < 10 m resolution)
candidate_sources.temporal_precision: Exact incident ignition time (minute-level precision: e.g. 04:12 CST) and fire duration (hours to days)
candidate_sources.download_api: Public incident investigations list (csb.gov/investigations); CSB Incident Wiki database; semi-structured PDF/HTML
candidate_sources.estimated_useful_events: 120+ catastrophic major industrial fires/explosions (1998–2024); approx. 15–25 events within active VIIRS operational era (2012–present)
candidate_sources.potential_circularity: NONE. Independent federal accident investigation reports with photographic, forensic, and SCADA documentation.
candidate_sources.major_limitations: Small event count. Major chemical disasters occur infrequently. Must intersect exact fire duration with daytime/nighttime VIIRS overpass window.
candidate_sources.recommended_use: HIGHEST QUALITY T1 INDUSTRIAL FIRE BENCHMARK. Every event is gold-standard ground truth, but must be manually curated.

candidate_sources.name: Major Accident Reporting System (eMARS)
candidate_sources.provider: European Commission Joint Research Centre (JRC) / European Environment Agency (EEA)
candidate_sources.geographic_coverage: European Union / OECD countries (Seveso III Directive sites)
candidate_sources.spatial_precision: Country / NUTS-2 administrative region only (facility name and GPS coordinates are REDACTED by law)
candidate_sources.download_api: European Industrial Emissions Portal web query / CSV export
candidate_sources.major_limitations: FATAL SPATIAL GAP. Under EU Seveso regulations, exact facility names and geographic coordinates are withheld for operator confidentiality and security. Cannot match against satellite pixel footprint.
candidate_sources.recommended_use: REJECTED FOR SPATIAL DATASET CONSTRUCTION. Unusable for FIRMS matching due to missing coordinates.

candidate_sources.name: ARIA Industrial Accident Database
candidate_sources.provider: Bureau for Analysis of Industrial Risks and Pollution (BARPI), French Ministry for Ecological Transition
candidate_sources.spatial_precision: Municipality name, department, industrial sector; exact coordinates available for selected classified installations (ICPE)
candidate_sources.download_api: aria.developpement-durable.gouv.fr query portal / ICPE open data registry
candidate_sources.estimated_useful_events: 50–100 major refinery and chemical warehouse fires with confirmed facility locations during VIIRS era
candidate_sources.major_limitations: Requires linking ARIA narrative reports to the French ICPE installation spatial registry to retrieve precise geocoordinates.
candidate_sources.recommended_use: SECONDARY T2 INDUSTRIAL FIRE SOURCE for European petrochemical and chemical facility fires.

candidate_sources.name: Petroleum and Explosives Safety Organization (PESO) Incident Reports
candidate_sources.provider: PESO, Ministry of Commerce and Industry, Government of India
candidate_sources.geographic_coverage: India (refineries, petrochemical plants, LPG/LNG terminals, chemical factories)
candidate_sources.spatial_precision: Facility name, city/district, state (requires manual geocoding to industrial plot)
candidate_sources.temporal_precision: Date of incident, narrative description of time/shift
candidate_sources.download_api: PDF annual reports published at peso.gov.in; no open API
candidate_sources.estimated_useful_events: 10–25 major refinery/chemical incidents per year across India
candidate_sources.potential_circularity: NONE. Independent statutory regulatory investigation records.
candidate_sources.major_limitations: Zero structured GIS coordinates. Locations are text facility names requiring manual GIS polygon lookup. Sub-day ignition times must be extracted from investigation narratives.
candidate_sources.recommended_use: HIGH-PRIORITY MANUAL CURATION TARGET for Indian industrial fires. Solves the geographic imbalance for industrial fires if matched to VIIRS overpasses.

candidate_sources.name: Marsh 100 Largest Losses in the Hydrocarbon Industry
candidate_sources.spatial_precision: Named facility, operating company, country, precise plant unit
candidate_sources.download_api: Published technical loss monograph (PDF / commercial insurance database)
candidate_sources.license_restrictions: Marsh Public Monograph / Fair Dealing Research
candidate_sources.estimated_useful_events: 100 catastrophic historic losses; approx. 20–30 major global refinery fires occurred during the VIIRS operational era (2012–2024)
candidate_sources.potential_circularity: NONE. Independent commercial loss underwriting and insurance audit data.
candidate_sources.major_limitations: Requires manual geocoding of refinery units and manual temporal cross-referencing against VIIRS overpass times.
candidate_sources.recommended_use: GLOBAL T2 GOLD-STANDARD BENCHMARK for major refinery unit fires (e.g. Philadelphia Energy Solutions refinery fire 2019, Deer Park ITC chemical fire 2019, Balikpapan refinery fire 2022).

candidate_sources.name: EOG Global Persistent Non-Flare Industrial Heat Sources
candidate_sources.provider: Earth Observation Group, Payne Institute, Colorado School of Mines
candidate_sources.geographic_coverage: Global (steel mills, blast furnaces, aluminum smelters, cement plants, brick kilns)
candidate_sources.download_api: EOG spatial layers / academic publications (Liu et al., Remote Sensing of Environment)
candidate_sources.potential_circularity: LOW. Derived from Nightfire Planck radiance fitting, separate from FIRMS I-band active fire pipeline.
candidate_sources.major_limitations: Continuous operational heat source, not an emergency fire or flare.
candidate_sources.recommended_use: CRITICAL NEGATIVE CLASS CANDIDATE: Allows defining an explicit 'INDUSTRIAL_PROCESS_HEAT' class to prevent false emergency fire alerts on routine hot manufacturing plants.
